Town of Mayodan
Municipal Accounting Services
(MAS) Program Celebration

May 11, 2026


           Municipal Accounting Services
                  (MAS) Program
• American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funding awarded to the State of North
  Carolina and then sub-awarded to NCLM.
• Funding covers MAS participant costs in the program for the first 3 years
  including software licensing, conversion, and maintenance costs as well as
  the cost of the accounting assistance through the end of 2026.
• Goal is to:
    • promote financial accountability and reliability by providing 1)
      governmental accounting software 2) guidance on best financial
      practices and 3) accounting assistance to ensure year-end audit
      readiness.
    • Provide software & accounting assistance for 40-60 Towns (<2500 pop.)
• Mayodan is the 28th town to convert to Black Mountain Software


                         Major Mayodan
                        Accomplishments
• Went “live” successfully on new financial software – June 1st, 2025.

• General Ledger was converted to the MAS Program Standard Uniform Chart of
  Accounts.

• Central Depository has been established, and bank accounts have been reduced from
  16 accounts to 4 accounts.

• Investments accounts have been reduced from 2 to 1.

• Town was sharing cash drawers among 3 members. A 2nd cash drawer was purchased,
  and staff was trained on managing cash drawers on a 1 to 1 basis.

• The Town implemented Positive Pay.


                       Major Mayodan
                      Accomplishments
• Bank Reconciliation module in BMS has improved bank reconciliation each
  month. Bank reconciliations were previously completed manually.

• The Interest Allocation feature in BMS has made distributing interest among the
  funds easier.

• The Payroll module in BMS has made payroll a smoother process than before.

• Went “live with Citizens portal, allowing citizens access to online payment
  options and past billing history.


More to Come…

• Continued mentoring of Staff / Board on Accounting related matters

• Implementation of Best Practices and Policies

• Available to Answer General Accounting Questions and MAS Help Desk

• Networking of municipalities that use the software to create a resource for
 units to share experiences and knowledge

• Financial management training opportunities for Board and Staff


More to Come…

• Manuals providing information on financial tasks that must be done on a
daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, and annual basis along with information on
how to complete those tasks.

• Consistent use of a Standard Chart of Accounts among participants could
lead to more efficient and cost-effective preparation of financial statements and
audits to assist with the amount of time it takes to complete an audit.


Equation for Financial Success

 Enhanced Software Tool Effectively Used by Staff
                      +
   MAS Accounting Assistance Program Efforts
                      +
   Regular Management and Board Oversight
                      =
         Reliable Financial Records
                     and
         Quality Services to Citizens

Item for Agenda:   Public Hearing and Decision – Ratification of Demolition Ordinance Adoption
                   (500 N. Third Avenue) and Resolution Confirming Demolition Charges and Lien

Meeting Date:      May 11, 2026

Placement on       Public Hearings
Agenda:

Presenter:         Melody Shuler, Town Manager

Description of     Background
Agenda Item or     The Town of Mayodan completed minimum housing enforcement for the
Other Pertinent    residential structure located at 500 N. 3rd Ave (PIN 120412), owned by the
Information for    Heirs, Known and Unknown, of Mary Lee Bryant Biggs and Roy C. Biggs.
Council:           Following an inspection on July 26, 2024, a complaint and notice of hearing
                   were served on March 28, 2025. A duly noticed hearing was held on June 26,
                   2025, before the Code Enforcement Officer.
                   On June 26, 2025, the Code Enforcement Officer issued an Order finding the
                   structure deteriorated/dilapidated and directing the owner to repair or
                   demolish the structure within ninety (90) days. No corrective action was taken.
                   At the November 10, 2025 Town Council meeting, the Council adopted a
                   Demolition Ordinance authorizing and directing the Ordinance Enforcement
                   Officer to demolish the structure and place a placard on the property. The
                   Ordinance was subsequently recorded in the Rockingham County Register of
                   Deeds on November 19, 2025 (Book 1701, Page 1757). The demolition has
                   since been completed.
                   Procedural Note
                   State law requires that before a demolition lien can be enforced, the governing
                   board must: (1) ratify by ordinance its prior adoption of the demolition
                   ordinance, and (2) confirm the associated costs by resolution in order to
                   establish a valid lien against the property for cost recovery. A public hearing is
                   required prior to these actions to provide the property owner and parties of
                   interest an opportunity to be heard. The public hearing was advertised
                   according to law.
                   Next Steps
                     • Following the public hearing, Council will consider ratification of the
                       Demolition Ordinance.
                     • Council will consider adoption of a Resolution confirming the demolition
                       charges and directing that a lien be filed against the property.
                     • The confirmed lien will be filed in the appropriate offices of the Town of
                       Mayodan and Rockingham County, including the Rockingham County
                       Clerk of Superior Court’s Office.


Requested Action
Following the public hearing, Council is requested to:
  1. Ratify the adoption of the Demolition Ordinance for the structure located
     at 500 N. 3rd Ave, Mayodan, NC 27027 (Parcel ID: 120412); and
  2. Adopt a Resolution confirming the demolition charges and directing that a
     lien be filed against the property in the amount of the actual cost of
     demolition.

Section 3. The cost of removal or demolition shall constitute a lien against the real property 500 N. 3rd Ave
Mayodan Mayodan NC 27027 Parcel ID: 120412 . The lien shall be filed in all appropriate offices of the Town of
Mayodan and Rockingham County, including the Rockingham County Clerk of Superior Court’s Office, and
shall have the same priority and be collected in the same manner as the lien for special assessments in Article 10
of G.S. Chapter 160A.

Section 4. Upon completion of the required removal or demolition, the Ordinance Enforcement Officer shall
determine whether any of the materials have re-sale value and if so, to make a reasonable effort to sell the same.
If any materials are sold, the Ordinance Enforcement Officer shall credit the process against the cost of removal
or demolition, and this shall be noted as such in the recorded lien. If a surplus remains after sale of the materials
and satisfaction of the cost of removal or demolition, the Ordinance Enforcement Officer shall deposit the
surplus in the Superior Court where it shall be secured and disbursed in the manner provided by Article 12 of
Chapter 160D of the General Statutes.

Section 5. It shall be unlawful for any person to remove or cause to be removed the placard referenced herein
and affixed to the structure. It shall likewise be unlawful for any person to occupy or to permit the occupancy
of any structure building therein declared to be unfit for human habitation.

Section 6. This ordinance shall become effective upon its adoption.

                       Resolution Confirming Demolition Charges and
                             Establishing Lien Against Property
                 500 N. 3rd Avenue, Mayodan, NC 27027 (Parcel ID: 120412)

WHEREAS, the Town of Mayodan completed minimum housing code enforcement proceedings
for the residential structure located at 500 N. 3rd Avenue, Mayodan, North Carolina 27027,
identified as Parcel ID 120412, and owned by Heirs, Known and Unknown, of Mary Lee Bryant
Biggs and Roy C. Biggs (the “Owner”); and

WHEREAS, following inspection, notice, and a duly noticed hearing on June 26, 2025, the Code
Enforcement Officer issued an Order finding the structure to be deteriorated and dilapidated and
directing the Owner to repair or demolish the structure within ninety (90) days; and

WHEREAS, no corrective action was taken by the Owner within the time prescribed; and

WHEREAS, on November 10, 2025, the Town Council of Mayodan adopted a Demolition
Ordinance authorizing and directing the Ordinance Enforcement Officer to remove or demolish
the structure, which Ordinance was recorded in the Rockingham County Register of Deeds on
November 19, 2025 at Book 1701, Page 1757; and

WHEREAS, the Town of Mayodan subsequently caused the demolition of the structure to be
completed, at an actual total cost of $10,535.00 (the “Demolition Cost”); and

WHEREAS, pursuant to G.S. § 160A-443(6) and Article 10 of G.S. Chapter 160A, the Town is
authorized to place a lien on the real property for the cost of demolition, which lien shall have the
same priority and be collected in the same manner as liens for special assessments; and

WHEREAS, a public hearing was duly held on May 11, 2026, providing the Owner and parties
of interest an opportunity to be heard regarding the demolition charges and the proposed lien; and

WHEREAS, the Town Council has ratified the adoption of the Demolition Ordinance and now
desires to confirm the demolition charges and direct that a lien be filed against the property.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, by the Town Council of the Town of Mayodan,
North Carolina, as follows:

Section 1. The Town Council hereby confirms that the total cost of demolition of the structure
located at 500 N. 3rd Avenue, Mayodan, NC 27027 (Parcel ID: 120412) is $10,535.00.


Section 2. The confirmed Demolition Cost of $10,535.00 shall constitute a lien against the real
property located at 500 N. 3rd Avenue, Mayodan, NC 27027 (Parcel ID: 120412), in the name of
Heirs, Known and Unknown, of Mary Lee Bryant Biggs and Roy C. Biggs.

Section 3. The Town Manager and Town Attorney are hereby directed to file the confirmed lien
in all appropriate offices of the Town of Mayodan and Rockingham County, including the
Rockingham County Clerk of Superior Court’s Office, in accordance with G.S. Chapter 160A,
Article 10.

Section 4. This Resolution shall become effective upon its adoption.


Adopted this 11th day of May 2026.

        Item or          Emerging land uses such as data centers and
                         large-scale solar energy systems have become
    Other Pertinent
                         increasingly common in North Carolina and
    Information for      surrounding regions. In response, Town Council
        Council:         requested that staff prepare temporary moratoria
                         to allow time to evaluate potential impacts and
                         develop appropriate regulatory standards.

                         The Town’s current Zoning Ordinance does not
                         include specific definitions or standards

                         Discussion
                         Data centers and similar high-impact facilities can
                         place significant demands on electrical

                         and backup systems. Large-scale solar energy
                         systems—particularly ground-mounted or
                         commercial installations—may also raise
                         concerns related to land use compatibility, site
                         design, and long-term maintenance.

                         Temporary moratoria are authorized under North
                         Carolina General Statute § 160D-107 and provide
                         a defined period for local governments to study
                         these uses and develop appropriate regulations.

                         The proposed moratoria would suspend the
                         acceptance and processing of development
                         approvals for these uses for sixty (60) days.
                         During this time, staff would prepare ordinance
                         amendments establishing definitions, identifying
                         appropriate zoning districts, and developing
                         development standards.

TOWN OF MAYODAN, NORTH CAROLINA
ORDINANCE ESTABLISHING A TEMPORARY MORATORIUM ON DEVELOPMENT
APPROVALS FOR DATA CENTERS AND OTHER HIGH-IMPACT FACILITIES


WHEREAS, the Town of Mayodan is authorized under N.C. General Statute § 160D-107 to
adopt temporary moratoria on development approvals in order to protect the public health, safety,
and welfare; and

WHEREAS, the Town has recently experienced increased interest and inquiries related to the
development of data centers, cryptocurrency mining operations, and other high-impact data
processing or energy-intensive facilities; and

WHEREAS, such uses may create substantial and unique impacts, including but not limited to
significant electrical demand and strain on local and regional utility infrastructure, noise impacts
from mechanical equipment and backup generators, high water consumption for cooling systems,
potential land use compatibility concerns with nearby residential or mixed-use areas, and
environmental and operational impacts not currently addressed in the Town’s development
regulations; and

WHEREAS, the Town’s current Zoning Ordinance does not contain specific definitions, use
classifications, or performance standards to adequately regulate these types of facilities; and

WHEREAS, the Town Council finds that immediate acceptance and approval of such
development applications without appropriate standards could negatively impact public
infrastructure, surrounding properties, and the overall character of the community; and

WHEREAS, the Town requires a limited period of time to study these uses and to develop
appropriate regulations, including use definitions, zoning district placement, and performance
standards; and

WHEREAS, a temporary moratorium is necessary to allow the Town sufficient time to
undertake this work in an orderly and deliberate manner within a compressed timeframe.


NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Town Council of the Town of Mayodan:

Section 1. Moratorium Established
A temporary moratorium is hereby established on the acceptance, processing, and approval of
any development approval required by law for the establishment, construction, expansion, or
modification of the following uses:



                                            Page 1 of 4


   •   Data Centers
   •   Cryptocurrency Mining Facilities
   •   Artificial Intelligence Processing Facilities
   •   High-Performance Computing Facilities
   •   Other similar high-impact data processing or energy-intensive uses, whether as a primary
       or accessory use
This includes, but is not limited to:
   •   Rezoning applications and zoning map amendments
   •   Conditional zoning or special use permits
   •   Site plan approvals
   •   Zoning permits or certificates of zoning compliance
   •   Any other development approval required by law and administered by the Town


Section 2. Applicability
This moratorium shall apply to all properties within the corporate limits of the Town of Mayodan
and its extraterritorial jurisdiction (ETJ), if applicable.


Section 3. Exemptions
The following shall be exempt from this moratorium:
   1. Any project that has received a complete and valid development approval prior to the
      effective date of this ordinance, consistent with N.C.G.S. § 160D-107(c);
   2. Routine maintenance, repair, or interior improvements to existing structures that do not
      increase the intensity or capacity of a use;
   3. Uses that are clearly incidental and accessory to a permitted principal use and do not
      meet the definition of a high-impact facility.


Section 4. Statement of Problems and Conditions Necessitating the Moratorium
The Town Council finds that this moratorium is necessary due to the following conditions:
   •   The Town’s development regulations do not currently address data centers or similar
       high-impact facilities;




                                            Page 2 of 4


   •   Such uses may place substantial and immediate demands on public utilities, including
       electricity and water systems;
   •   These uses may generate noise and other impacts incompatible with nearby residential
       and commercial areas; and
   •   Without appropriate standards in place, approval of such development could result in
       adverse impacts that cannot be adequately mitigated under existing regulations.


Section 5. Plan of Action
During the period of the moratorium, the Town shall undertake the following actions, which will
be initiated immediately upon adoption of this ordinance and pursued on an expedited schedule:
   1. Develop and adopt definitions for data centers and related high-impact facilities;
   2. Evaluate and establish appropriate zoning districts where such uses may be permitted,
      conditionally permitted, or prohibited;
   3. Draft and consider development standards, including but not limited to:
           o   Noise limitations
           o   Setbacks and buffering requirements
           o   Utility capacity and infrastructure impacts
           o   Site design and operational characteristics;
   4. Submit proposed text amendments to the Planning Board for review and
      recommendation; and
   5. Conduct required public hearings and consider adoption of ordinance amendments by the
      Town Council.


Section 6. Duration
This moratorium shall remain in effect for a period of sixty (60) days from the date of adoption,
unless:
   •   Repealed earlier by the Town Council; or
   •   Extended in accordance with applicable law.
The Town Council finds that this duration is reasonably necessary to complete the initial study,
draft ordinance amendments, and begin the public review process within an expedited timeframe.




                                           Page 3 of 4


Section 7. Severability
If any provision of this ordinance is held invalid, such invalidity shall not affect the remaining
provisions.


Section 8. Effective Date
This ordinance shall become effective upon adoption.


ADOPTED this ____ day of __________, 2026.




                                                    ________________________________
                                                                                    E. Dwight Lake
                                                                                              Mayor

TOWN OF MAYODAN, NORTH CAROLINA

ORDINANCE ESTABLISHING A TEMPORARY MORATORIUM ON DEVELOPMENT
APPROVALS FOR CERTAIN SOLAR ENERGY SYSTEMS



WHEREAS, the Town of Mayodan is authorized under N.C. General Statute § 160D-107 to
adopt temporary moratoria on development approvals in order to protect the public health, safety,
and welfare; and

WHEREAS, the Town has recently experienced increased interest and inquiries related to the
development of utility-scale solar energy systems, commercial solar installations, and other
medium- to large-scale solar energy facilities; and

WHEREAS, such uses may create substantial and unique impacts, including but not limited to
land use compatibility concerns, visual impacts, stormwater runoff, glare, buffering and
screening issues, and potential impacts to adjacent residential, agricultural, and commercial
properties; and

WHEREAS, the Town is also experiencing the installation of solar energy systems associated
with commercial and industrial developments, including parking lot canopy systems and other
ground-mounted arrays that may function at a scale greater than typical accessory uses; and

WHEREAS, the Town’s current Zoning Ordinance does not contain specific definitions, use
classifications, or performance standards to adequately regulate solar energy systems of varying
scales and intensities; and

WHEREAS, the Town Council finds that immediate acceptance and approval of such
development applications without appropriate standards could negatively impact surrounding
properties, the built environment, and the overall character of the community; and

WHEREAS, the Town requires a limited period of time to study these uses and to develop
appropriate regulations, including use definitions, zoning district placement, and performance
standards; and

WHEREAS, a temporary moratorium is necessary to allow the Town sufficient time to
undertake this work in an orderly and deliberate manner within a compressed timeframe; and

WHEREAS, this moratorium is not intended to prohibit or impair the reasonable use of solar
energy systems serving residential properties as protected under N.C. General Statute § 160D-
914.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED by the Town Council of the Town of Mayodan:


                                           Page 1 of 4


Section 1. Moratorium Established

A temporary moratorium is hereby established on the acceptance, processing, and approval of
any development approval required by law for the establishment, construction, expansion, or
modification of the following uses:

   •   Utility-scale solar energy systems (solar farms or solar power plants)

   •   Commercial solar energy systems, including ground-mounted systems and solar canopy
       or carport-mounted systems associated with non-residential uses

   •   Other similar medium- to large-scale solar energy systems, whether as a primary or
       accessory use, that exceed the thresholds described below

For purposes of this section, the moratorium shall apply to solar energy systems that meet one or
more of the following criteria:
   •   Have a total rated capacity greater than 25 kilowatts (kW); or

   •   Occupy more than 1,000 square feet of surface area; or

   •   Are ground-mounted or canopy-mounted and are not attached to a principal building

This includes, but is not limited to:
   •   Rezoning applications and zoning map amendments
   •   Conditional zoning or special use permits
   •   Site plan approvals
   •   Zoning permits or certificates of zoning compliance
   •   Any other development approval required by law and administered by the Town


Section 2. Applicability

This moratorium shall apply to all properties within the corporate limits of the Town of Mayodan
and its extraterritorial jurisdiction (ETJ), if applicable.



Section 3. Exemptions

The following shall be exempt from this moratorium:

   1. Any project that has received a complete and valid development approval prior to the
      effective date of this ordinance, consistent with N.C.G.S. § 160D-107(c);




                                           Page 2 of 4


   2. Accessory solar energy systems serving residential uses, including roof-mounted or
      ground-mounted systems that are incidental to a dwelling unit and serve on-site
      residential consumption;

   3. Roof-mounted solar energy systems attached to an existing principal building that:

           o   Serve on-site consumption; and

           o   Do not exceed 25 kW in total capacity;

   4. Routine maintenance, repair, or replacement of existing solar energy systems that do not
      increase the size, footprint, or generating capacity of the system.



Section 4. Statement of Problems and Conditions Necessitating the Moratorium

The Town Council finds that this moratorium is necessary due to the following conditions:
   •   The Town’s development regulations do not currently address solar energy systems of
       varying scales;

   •   Utility-scale and commercial solar installations may create land use, visual, and
       environmental impacts not addressed by existing regulations;

   •   Medium-scale systems associated with commercial and industrial uses, including parking
       lot solar canopies, may function at an intensity greater than typical accessory uses; and

   •   Without appropriate standards in place, approval of such development could result in
       adverse impacts that cannot be adequately mitigated under existing regulations.



Section 5. Plan of Action
During the period of the moratorium, the Town shall undertake the following actions, which will
be initiated immediately upon adoption of this ordinance and pursued on an expedited schedule:

   1. Develop and adopt definitions for solar energy systems based on scale and use;
   2. Evaluate and establish appropriate zoning districts where solar energy systems may be
      permitted, conditionally permitted, or prohibited;
   3. Draft and consider development standards, including but not limited to:
           o   Setbacks and buffering requirements

           o   Height limitations

           o   Glare mitigation


                                           Page 3 of 4


           o   Stormwater and environmental considerations

           o   Decommissioning and abandonment requirements

           o   Design and operational characteristics

   4. Submit proposed text amendments to the Planning Board for review and
      recommendation; and

   5. Conduct required public hearings and consider adoption of ordinance amendments by the
      Town Council.



Section 6. Duration
This moratorium shall remain in effect for a period of sixty (60) days from the date of adoption,
unless:
   •   Repealed earlier by the Town Council; or
   •   Extended in accordance with applicable law

The Town Council finds that this duration is reasonably necessary to complete the initial study,
draft ordinance amendments, and begin the public review process within an expedited timeframe.



Section 7. Severability

If any provision of this ordinance is held invalid, such invalidity shall not affect the remaining
provisions.



Section 8. Effective Date

This ordinance shall become effective upon adoption.



ADOPTED this ____ day of __________, 2026.

NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARING
Town of Mayodan
Notice is hereby given that the Mayodan Town Council will hold a public hearing
on Monday, May 13, 2026, at 6:00 p.m. at the James A. Collins Municipal Building, 210 W.
Main Street, Mayodan, North Carolina.
The purpose of this hearing is to receive public comment on the proposed adoption of
a temporary 60-day moratorium on the acceptance and processing of applications for
solar farm developments and data center developments within the Town of Mayodan’s
jurisdiction. The moratorium is intended to allow the Town sufficient time to review and
consider potential amendments to the Town’s zoning ordinance and development
regulations related to these uses.
All interested citizens are invited to attend and be heard.
For additional information, please contact Mayodan Town Hall during normal business
hours at (336) 427-0241.

Town of Mayodan Zoning
Special Use Case # SU-002-2026
Staff Report: Melody Shuler, Town Manager
Applicant:     Forbes Realty Consultants, Ken Mackovic Jr.
Owner:         Diane Best Purgason
Location:      N 7th Avenue (end of roadway)
GIS ID #:      791715543127; Parcel 167889
Request:       Special Use Permit to allow alternative street and pedestrian design (open-section streets
               in lieu of curb and gutter and no sidewalks)


Explanation of the Request:
SU-002-2026 is a request by applicant Ken Mackovic Jr. for a Special Use Permit to allow an alternative
street and pedestrian design for a proposed single-family residential subdivision located off N 7th Avenue
in the R-12 Residential Zoning District.

The proposed development consists of single-family residential lots, which are permitted by right in the
R-12 district. The Special Use Permit is required to allow deviations from traditional street design
standards, specifically the use of open-section streets (ditch sections with reduced pavement width) in lieu
of curb and gutter, and the omission of sidewalks or other pedestrian facilities.

Background:
The Town of Mayodan Zoning Ordinance currently requires streets to be constructed to NCDOT standards
and does not explicitly provide flexibility for alternative street cross-sections or pedestrian
accommodations.

To address this, the Town is concurrently considering Text Amendment TA-001-2026, which would
establish Section 5.25 – Alternative Street and Pedestrian Design Standards. This amendment would allow
for open-section streets and alternative pedestrian accommodations where appropriate.

The Special Use Permit request is contingent upon adoption of the text amendment and is intended to
apply those provisions to this specific development.

Location/Current Land Use:
The subject property consists of vacant land located at the terminus of N 7th Avenue. The site is partially
wooded and includes areas within the Mayo River WS-IV Critical Area.

Condition and Land Use of Surrounding Properties:
   •   North: Vacant / residential, zoned R-12 (Residential Low Density)
   •   South: Residential / town water treatment plant, zoned R-12 (Residential Low Density)
   •   East: Vacant / residential, zoned R-12 (Residential Low Density)
   •   West: Vacant / residential, zoned R-12 (Residential Low Density)


Special Use Permit Requirements:
The proper public hearing notices were sent by staff to all adjacent property owners and a sign was placed
on the subject property site at least 10 days prior to the date of the meeting.
The following should be considered when evaluating a special use permit application:
   1. Will the proposed use materially endanger the public health or safety?
   2. Will the proposed use comply with all regulations and standards generally applicable within the
      zoning district and specifically applicable to the particular type of special use or class of special
      uses?
   3. Will the proposed use substantially injure the value of adjoining property?
   4. Will the proposed use be in harmony with the area in which it is located?

Conditions may be attached to a Special Use Permit and must be agreed to in writing by both parties.

Analysis:
Use and Zoning
The proposed single-family residential use is permitted by right in the R-12 zoning district. The Special
Use Permit request is limited to alternative infrastructure design standards and does not involve a change
in land use.

Alternative Street Design
The applicant proposes an open-section street design utilizing roadside ditches and reduced pavement
width in lieu of curb and gutter.

The proposed design is consistent with the rural character of the surrounding area and is appropriate for a
low-density residential development. Final roadway design, including pavement width, cross-section, and
materials, will be subject to Technical Review Committee review and approval.

Pedestrian Facilities
No sidewalks or alternative pedestrian facilities are proposed.

There are no existing sidewalks or pedestrian facilities along N 7th Avenue, and the Draft Rockingham
County Comprehensive Transportation Plan does not identify planned pedestrian improvements in this
area.

Based on the absence of existing or planned pedestrian connectivity, staff finds that no reasonable
opportunity for pedestrian connection exists, and therefore a sidewalk or alternative pedestrian facility is
not required.

Watershed Compliance
A portion of the site is located within the Mayo River WS-IV Critical Area. The ordinance requires a
minimum lot size of one-half (½) acre within this area.

Public Safety and Access
The Fire Chief reviewed the proposed site plan and indicated that, while the current layout would allow
for adequate emergency response, the presence of a single point of ingress and egress is a concern. Due


to the potential limitations this may place on emergency access, the Fire Chief recommends consideration
of a secondary access point to improve response capabilities and overall site safety. If feasible, an
additional connection from Utility Street near the Town maintenance facility could be explored, including
the option of limiting such access to emergency use only. The Fire Chief also noted that the proposed
roadway widths, cul-de-sac dimensions, and fire hydrant placement appear adequate, and that on-street
parking should be manageable provided the minimum roadway width is maintained.

Drainage
The proposed open-section street design relies on ditch drainage. The applicant’s engineer has indicated
that the proposed roadway and ditch system is expected to meet applicable NCDOT and Town standards
for drainage. A drainage plan prepared by a licensed engineer will be required to demonstrate that
stormwater will be adequately managed without adverse impacts to adjacent properties. Final engineering
will be completed and reviewed through the Technical Review Committee and NCDOT review processes
in accordance with applicable regulations and standards to protect public health, safety, and welfare.

Staff Recommendation:
Staff recommends approval of SU-002-2026, a request for a Special Use Permit to allow alternative street
and pedestrian design for a single-family residential development in the R-12 zoning district, subject to
the following conditions:

   1. All alternative street designs shall comply with Section 5.25 – Alternative Street and Pedestrian
      Design Standards, if adopted.
   2. Final roadway design shall demonstrate adequate access of twenty (20) feet in width for emergency
      vehicles and maintained with applicable fire code requirements.
   3. A drainage plan shall be prepared by a licensed engineer demonstrating that the proposed open-
      section street and ditch system will adequately manage stormwater and not create adverse impacts
      to adjacent properties. Final drainage design shall be subject to Technical Review Committee
      approval.
   4. The applicant shall obtain all required erosion and sedimentation control permits from the
      appropriate regulatory authority prior to land disturbance.
   5. All utility infrastructure and connections shall be reviewed and approved by the Town prior to
      final plat approval.
   6. The development shall be subject to Technical Review Committee review prior to final plat
      approval. All comments and required revisions identified through the TRC process shall be
      addressed to the satisfaction of the Town.

The applicant has agreed to the proposed conditions in writing.

Planning Board:
The Planning Board reviewed the special use permit application on April 20, 2026, and approved a motion
for a favorable recommendation of SU-002-2026 with the above conditions. Motion passed 4:2 with
Norma O’Steen and Sammy Martin in opposition.

Member O'Steen expressed comfort with the existing ordinance language and raised concerns about the
quality of housing construction, while Member Martin opposed the alternative infrastructure standard.


Requested Action:
   •   Motion to approve Special Use Permit SUP-002-2026 with the recommended conditions, based
       on an affirmative determination of the required findings of fact.

Findings of Fact:
   •   Finding #1: The proposed use will not materially endanger the public health or safety.
   •   Finding #2: The proposed use will comply with all regulations and standards generally applicable
       within the zoning district and specifically applicable to the particular type of special use or class
       of special uses.
   •   Finding #3: The proposed use will not substantially injure the value of adjoining property.
   •   Finding #4: The proposed use will be in harmony with the area in which it is located.

                MAYODAN PLANNING AND ZONING BOARD/BOARD OF ADJUSTMENT
                                 April 20, 2026 MEETING
                                   210 W Main Street
                                        6:00 P.M.

Members Present:                                Staff Present:

Tom Watford – Chairman

Norma O’Steen called the meeting to order at 6:03 p.m.

Approval of Minutes:
Upon a motion by Tania Carter, seconded by Amanda Joyce, the Board voted unanimously (6:0) to
approve the minutes of the March 19, 2026 meeting.

New Business:
Text Amendment TA-001-2026: Alternative Street and Pedestrian Design Standards
Melody Shuler, Town Manager, presented the Text Amendment application for alternative street and
pedestrian design standards. The application seeks to allow alternative infrastructure configurations—
specifically ribbon asphalt with open swale ditches in lieu of curb, gutter, and sidewalks—for new
residential development in appropriate circumstances.

The applicant’s representative, Ken, provided background on the proposed development, noting that the
subject property is a timbered parcel zoned R-12 requiring single-family residential use with minimum
12,000 square foot lots and 100-foot-wide lots. The targeted price point for homes is $400,000–$450,000
with approximately 2,000 square feet. He explained that the current town ordinance requires curb, gutter,
stormwater infrastructure, and sidewalks, which would increase development costs from approximately
$400 per linear foot to $1,000 per linear foot—roughly $1,000,000 total, or approximately $15,000 per lot
before engineering costs. He noted that the development could not be financially viable under those
requirements and that rezoning for smaller lots and higher density would otherwise need to be
considered. The proposed infrastructure would use ribbon asphalt construction with open swale drainage,
which would still require engineering review and approvals from NCDOT, NCDENR, and the Town.

Ken further noted that N 7th Avenue would serve as the sole access point to the development and is
currently 18 feet wide. The existing right-of-way on Utility Street measures 47 feet, which is below the
NCDOT minimum of 50 feet; he stated that additional right-of-way acquisition would be required for any


access improvements at that location. He noted the proposed drawings are preliminary and subject to
modification.

Public comments and Board discussion followed. A citizen (Connie) expressed concern about drainage
conditions on N 7th Avenue, noting that drainage in the area has worsened over the past several years,
that heavy rain events create significant runoff past her property, and that she would like to see street
improvements made prior to any new traffic being added to the corridor. She indicated that improper
grading of prior curb and gutter installation on Wilkins Street had negatively impacted her property. She
stated she desired higher-end housing in Mayodan but wanted stormwater and road conditions addressed
properly.

Another citizen (Emma Jean) stated she had no objection to the text amendment provided that proper
grading, stormwater management, and street improvements were incorporated, including widening of N
7th Avenue.

Board members discussed the item at length. Member Shelton noted the development’s connection to
Utility Street and confirmed that curb and gutter infrastructure is not currently present along the corridor.
Members Menard and Shelton expressed support for the text amendment, noting the cost implications
and the need to incentivize development of higher-quality housing in Mayodan. Member Menard
suggested the Town consider absorbing the cost of extending curb and gutter along N 7th Avenue as a
public road improvement to accommodate future development. Members Carter and Joyce also
expressed support, with Member Joyce noting that a prior development on Turner Road had been denied
because they didn’t have curb and gutter, and that stormwater management in the area is a broader Town
infrastructure issue. She noted that the absence of an alternative standard would likely deter future
residential development.

Members O’Steen and Martin expressed opposition. Member O’Steen stated she was comfortable with
the existing text and expressed concern about the quality of housing construction. Member Martin was
not in favor of the alternative standard. The Town Attorney (Eugene) clarified that adoption of a text
amendment does not create a cause of action or legal liability, and that any existing developer could apply
for their project to be considered under the new standard on an equal basis.

Motion was made by Charles Menard and seconded by Ed Shelton to send a favorable recommendation
to the Town Council for the text amendment request for curb, gutter, and sidewalk alternatives. Motion
carried 4:2 with Norma O’Steen and Sammy Martin in opposition.

Special Use Permit SUP-002-2026: Curb, Gutter, & Sidewalk Alternative for N 7th Avenue
Ms. Shuler noted that this item was related to the text amendment and had been discussed in depth
during the preceding agenda item. The Board proceeded to a vote.

Motion was made by Charles Menard and seconded by Ed Shelton to send a favorable recommendation
to the Town Council for the special use permit request for curb, gutter, and sidewalk alternatives at N 7th
Avenue. Motion carried 4:2 with Norma O’Steen and Sammy Martin in opposition.


Discussion:
Ms. Shuler noted a text amendment will be coming forward for data centers and solar farms.

Adjourn:
At 7:25 pm, a motion to adjourn was made by Ed Shelton, seconded by Charles Menard, and approved
unanimously (6:0).


 WRITTEN DECISION - SPECIAL USE PERMIT FOR ALTERNATIVE STREET AND
                PEDESTRIAN DESIGN - N 7TH AVENUE

WHEREAS, an application was submitted by Forbes Realty Consultants, Ken Mackovic Jr.,
requesting a Special Use Permit to allow alternative street and pedestrian design for a proposed
single-family residential subdivision at property located at N 7th Avenue (GIS ID: 791715543127;
Parcel 167889); and

WHEREAS, the subject property is located within the R-12 Residential (Low Density) zoning
district, where single-family residential use is permitted by right and the requested alternative
street and pedestrian design standards are permitted pursuant to a Special Use under the Town of
Mayodan Zoning Ordinance; and

WHEREAS, the application proposes the use of open-section streets (ditch sections with reduced
pavement width) in lieu of curb and gutter, and the omission of sidewalks for a single-family
residential subdivision on currently vacant, partially wooded land within the Mayo River WS-IV
Critical Area; and
WHEREAS, notice of the public hearing was duly provided in accordance with applicable law,
and a public hearing was held by the Town Council at which all persons wishing to be heard were
given the opportunity, and all competent, material, and substantial evidence was received; and

WHEREAS, the Planning Board reviewed the application on April 20, 2026, and voted 4:2 to
recommend approval of the Special Use Permit with conditions; and

WHEREAS, the Town Council, having considered the application, staff report, Planning Board
recommendation, and all evidence presented, makes the following findings in accordance with
N.C.G.S. § 160D-705(c):



FINDINGS OF FACT

   1. Public Health and Safety
      The proposed use will not materially endanger the public health or safety. The proposed
      roadway widths, cul-de-sac dimensions, and fire hydrant placement are adequate for
      emergency response. Adequate provisions for access, stormwater management, erosion
      control, and utility infrastructure can be met through compliance with applicable codes
      and the conditions imposed herein.

   2. Compliance with Ordinance Standards
      The proposed development complies with all applicable requirements of the Town of
      Mayodan Zoning Ordinance for the R-12 district, and the alternative street and pedestrian
      design standards are consistent with the provisions of proposed Text Amendment TA-
      001-2026 (Section 5.25 – Alternative Street and Pedestrian Design Standards). The


       Special Use Permit is contingent upon adoption of that text amendment and is capable of
       meeting all applicable development standards.

   3. Impact on Adjacent Property Values
      The proposed use will not substantially injure the value of adjoining properties. The
      surrounding area consists of vacant and residential properties in the R-12 zoning district,
      and the proposed single-family residential subdivision utilizing open-section street design
      is consistent with the low-density rural character of the area.

   4. Harmony with Surrounding Area
      The proposed use is in harmony with the area in which it is located. The open-section
      street design reflects the rural character of the surrounding neighborhood along N 7th
      Avenue, where no existing sidewalks or pedestrian facilities are present and no planned
      pedestrian improvements are identified in the Draft Rockingham County Comprehensive
      Transportation Plan. The development is consistent with the zoning designation and
      surrounding land uses.


NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED
That the Town of Mayodan Town Council hereby APPROVES Special Use Permit SU-002-2026
for property located at N 7th Avenue, to allow alternative street and pedestrian design for a single-
family residential subdivision, as shown on the site plan submitted with the application, subject to
the following conditions:



CONDITIONS

   1. Alternative Street Design Standards
      All alternative street designs shall comply with Section 5.25 – Alternative Street and
      Pedestrian Design Standards, if adopted.

   2. Fire and Emergency Access
      Final roadway design shall demonstrate adequate access of twenty (20) feet in width for
      emergency vehicles and maintained in accordance with applicable fire code requirements.

   3. Drainage Plan
      A drainage plan shall be prepared by a licensed engineer demonstrating that the proposed
      open-section street and ditch system will adequately manage stormwater and not create
      adverse impacts to adjacent properties. Final drainage design shall be subject to Technical
      Review Committee approval.


   4. Erosion and Sedimentation Control
      The applicant shall obtain all required erosion and sedimentation control permits from the
      appropriate regulatory authority prior to land disturbance.

   5. Utility Infrastructure
      All utility infrastructure and connections shall be reviewed and approved by the Town
      prior to final plat approval.

   6. Technical Review Committee
      The development shall be subject to Technical Review Committee review prior to final
      plat approval. All comments and required revisions identified through the TRC process
      shall be addressed to the satisfaction of the Town.



Adopted this 11th day of May 2026.

Town of Mayodan Zoning
Text Amendment Case # TA-001-2026
Staff Report: Melody Shuler, Town Manager
Applicant: Ken Mackovic Jr.

Background
The Town of Mayodan’s Zoning Ordinance currently requires streets to be constructed to North Carolina
Department of Transportation (NCDOT) standards and does not explicitly provide flexibility for
alternative street cross-sections or pedestrian accommodations.

As development patterns evolve and the Town seeks to balance infrastructure costs, rural character, and
environmental considerations, it is appropriate to allow alternative design options where traditional
curb/gutter and sidewalk construction may not be necessary or practical.

This amendment introduces flexibility for the use of open-section streets (ditch sections) and alternative
pedestrian facilities, while ensuring that public safety, drainage, and connectivity are maintained.

Proposed Text Change
Article VI – Special Uses and Development Standards
Add New Section 5.25 – Alternative Street and Pedestrian Design Standards

5.25 Alternative Street and Pedestrian Design Standards
a. Purpose
The purpose of this section is to provide flexibility in the design of streets and pedestrian facilities in
order to:
    • Reduce infrastructure costs
    • Preserve rural character
    • Promote environmentally sensitive design
    • Maintain safe and functional transportation networks

b. Alternative to Curb and Gutter (Open Section Streets)
In lieu of curb and gutter, the Town may approve open-section streets utilizing roadside ditches for
drainage, provided that:
     1. The design is prepared and certified by a licensed engineer;
     2. Adequate drainage is provided to prevent flooding, erosion, or standing water;
     3. Soil stabilization and erosion control measures are implemented;
     4. The street design is appropriate for the proposed development pattern and density, and
        demonstrates that an alternative design will function as well as or better than traditional curb and
        gutter in terms of drainage, safety, and maintenance;
     5. The street serves low-density residential development, rural areas, or areas where curb and gutter
        is not necessary for stormwater management;
     6. The design meets applicable NCDOT minimum construction standards unless otherwise approved
        by the Town;
     7. The Fire Chief and Public Works Director have reviewed and approved the design for access and
        maintenance purposes.
     8. Alternative street designs may include narrow pavement sections, rural street cross-sections, or
        reduced-width asphalt roadways (commonly referred to as ribbon-style pavement), where
        appropriate for low-volume residential development;


   9. The proposed street design shall demonstrate adequate access for emergency vehicles, including
      minimum travel widths, turning radii, and all-weather surface conditions sufficient to serve fire
      and emergency response needs.

c. Alternative to Sidewalks
In lieu of traditional sidewalks, the Town may approve alternative pedestrian accommodations, provided
that pedestrian connectivity and safety are maintained where a reasonable connection exists or is
planned. Acceptable alternatives may include:
     1. Multi-use paths (minimum 8 feet in width);
     2. Side paths or shared-use paths located within or adjacent to the right-of-way;
     3. Trails, greenways, or other off-street pedestrian facilities;
     4. Widened shoulders (minimum 4 feet) where appropriate;
     5. Internal pedestrian circulation systems that connect to existing or planned networks.

Where no existing or planned pedestrian facilities are present, and no reasonable opportunity for
connectivity exists, the Town may determine that no sidewalk, path, or pedestrian facility is required.

In making this determination, the Town may consider adopted plans, including but not limited to
comprehensive transportation plans, greenway plans, or other officially adopted infrastructure planning
documents.

d. Approval Criteria
Alternative street and pedestrian designs may be approved by the Town as part of site plan, subdivision,
or special use review upon finding that:
    1. The alternative design provides equal or better public safety than traditional curb, gutter, and
        sidewalk infrastructure;
    2. The design is consistent with the Town’s Land Development Plan and any adopted transportation
        or greenway plans;
    3. The alternative supports connectivity to adjacent properties or future development where
        applicable;
    4. Maintenance responsibilities are clearly defined;
    5. The design will not create adverse impacts to adjoining properties;
    6. The design provides adequate access for emergency services and will not impair fire protection
        or public safety response.

e. Limitations
    1. Alternative designs shall not be permitted where curb and gutter or sidewalks are necessary to
       address:
           o High traffic volumes
           o Safety concerns
           o Stormwater management constraints

Compatibility with Adopted Plans
The proposed amendment is consistent with the Town of Mayodan Land Development Plan and maintains
the Town’s commitment to safe, functional, and well-designed infrastructure. The amendment allows for
consideration of alternative street design approaches where appropriate, while preserving the Town’s
ability to require traditional improvements when necessary. This ensures development remains compatible
with existing and future land use patterns while supporting measured growth.


Staff Comments
This amendment provides a practical tool for the Town to evaluate development on a case-by-case basis.
It maintains appropriate safeguards while allowing flexibility that is more consistent with Mayodan’s scale
and development patterns.

Public Notice
The proper public hearing notices were provided for the text amendment.

Planning Board Recommendation
The Planning Board reviewed the text amendment application on April 20, 2026, and approved a motion
for a favorable recommendation of TA-001-2026. Motion passed 4:2 with Norma O’Steen and Sammy
Martin in opposition.

Member O'Steen expressed comfort with the existing ordinance language and raised concerns about the
quality of housing construction, while Member Martin opposed the alternative infrastructure standard.

Reasonableness and Consistency Statement
The proposed text amendment is reasonable and in the public interest as it allows for flexibility in street
design where appropriate, while maintaining the Town’s ability to ensure safe and functional
infrastructure. The amendment does not remove existing standards but provides an alternative approach
that may be applied based on specific site conditions.

The amendment is consistent with the Town of Mayodan Land Development Plan and supports the Town’s
goals of managed growth and compatible development. It ensures that new development can proceed in a
manner that is both practical and aligned with the Town’s adopted policies.

Requested Action
A motion to approve Text Amendment TA-001-2026 and the Reasonableness and Consistency Statement
as presented.

Item for Agenda:   Flood Damage Prevention Ordinance – First Reading (Introduction)

Placement on       New Business
Agenda:

Presenter:         Melody Schuler, Town Manager

Description of     Background
Agenda Item or     On December 10, 2025, the Town of Mayodan received a final flood hazard
Other Pertinent    determination letter from the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA)
Information for    notifying the Town that updated Flood Insurance Rate Maps (FIRMs) and a
Council:           Flood Insurance Study (FIS) report for Rockingham County will become
                   effective on June 10, 2026.
                   As a condition of continued eligibility in the National Flood Insurance Program
                   (NFIP), the Town is required to adopt floodplain management regulations that
                   meet or exceed the standards of 44 CFR Part 60.3(d) prior to the June 10, 2026
                   effective date. Communities that fail to enact the required regulations risk
                   suspension from the NFIP, which would prohibit residents from obtaining
                   federally backed flood insurance.
                   North Carolina has updated its model Flood Damage Prevention Ordinance to
                   reflect the new FIRM and FIS data and current NFIP requirements. The
                   attached draft ordinance is based on the updated state model and has been
                   prepared to bring the Town into compliance with both state and federal
                   floodplain management standards.
                   Procedural Note
                   Because the ordinance includes a criminal penalty provision, North Carolina
                   General Statute § 160A-175 requires that it be introduced at one meeting and
                   formally adopted at a subsequent meeting. Additionally, NCGS § 160D-601
                   requires that a public hearing notice be published in a newspaper of general
                   circulation once a week for two successive calendar weeks, with the first
                   publication not less than 10 days nor more than 25 days before the hearing
                   date.
                   Tonight’s action is the formal introduction of the ordinance. A public hearing and
                   vote on adoption will be scheduled at the June 8th meeting to allow sufficient
                   time for required public notice.
                   Next Steps
                       •   Staff will publish the required public hearing notice in the newspaper for
                           two successive weeks.
                       •   A public hearing and second reading for adoption will be scheduled at
                           the next available Council meeting, prior to the June 10, 2026 FIRM
                           effective date.
                       •   Upon adoption, the ordinance and supporting documentation will be
                           submitted to the NC Division of Emergency Management and FEMA
                           Region 4.
                   Requested Action
                   Council is requested to receive the Flood Damage Prevention Ordinance for a
                   first reading and introduction. Council should direct staff to proceed with
                   scheduling the required public hearing and second reading for adoption at the
                   June 8th meeting.
