        Potential Funding Sources—Local, State, or Federal sources of funds are noted here,
            where applicable.
        Implementation Schedule—Date by which the action the action should be completed.
         More information is provided when possible.
        Implementation Status (2025)—Indication of completion, progress, deferment, or no
         change since the previous plan. If the action is new, that will be noted here.

                   RESOLUTION TO ADOPT THE
      NORTHERN PIEDMONT REGIONAL HAZARD MITIGATION PLAN

WHEREAS, Rockingham County is vulnerable to an array of natural hazards that can cause loss
of life and damages to public and private property; and

WHEREAS, the Rockingham County desires to seek ways to mitigate situations that may
aggravate such circumstances; and

WHEREAS, the development and implementation of a hazard mitigation plan can result in
actions that reduce the long-term risk to life and property from natural hazards; and

WHEREAS, it is the intent of the Rockingham County Board of County Commissioners to
protect its citizens and property from the effects of natural hazards by preparing and maintaining
a local hazard mitigation plan; and

WHEREAS, the Legislature of the State of North Carolina has in Article 5, Section 160D-501 of
Chapter 160D of the North Carolina General Statutes, delegated to local governmental units the
responsibility to adopt regulations designed to promote the public health, safety, and general
welfare of its citizenry; and

WHEREAS, the Legislature of the State of North Carolina has enacted General Statute Section
166A-19.41 (State emergency assistance funds) which provides that for a state of emergency
declared pursuant to G.S. 166A-19.20(a) after the deadline established by the Federal Emergency
Management Agency pursuant to the Disaster Mitigation Act of 2002, P.L. 106-390, the eligible
entity shall have a hazard mitigation plan approved pursuant to the Stafford Act; and.

WHEREAS, Section 322 of the Federal Disaster Mitigation Act of 2000 states that local
governments must develop an All-Hazards Mitigation Plan in order to be eligible to receive future
Hazard Mitigation Grant Program Funds and other disaster-related assistance funding and that
said Plan must be updated and adopted within a five-year cycle; and

WHEREAS, Rockingham County in coordination with Caswell, Davie, Forsyth, Rockingham,
Stokes, Surry and Yadkin Counties and the participating municipalities within those Counties has
prepared a multi-jurisdictional hazard mitigation plan with input from the appropriate local and
state officials;

WHEREAS, Rockingham County has performed a comprehensive review and evaluation of each
section of the previously approved Hazard Mitigation Plan and has updated the said plan as
required under regulations at 44 CFR Part 201 and according to guidance issued by the Federal
Emergency Management Agency and the North Carolina Division of Emergency Management.

WHEREAS, it is the intent of the Board of Commissioners of Rockingham County to fulfill this
obligation in order that Rockingham County will be eligible for federal and state assistance in the
event that a state of disaster is declared for a hazard event affecting the jurisdiction;

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that the Board of County Commissioners of
Rockingham County hereby:

        1. Adopts the Northern Piedmont Regional Hazard Mitigation Plan; and


       2. Agrees to take such other official action as may be reasonably necessary to carry out
          the proposed actions of the Plan.

Adopted on ___________________, 2025.

                                                   ____________________________________
                                                                                  , Chair
                                                              LOCAL GOVERNING BODY
ATTEST:

___________________________
                  , Clerk

                 Town of Mayodan Social Media Policy
Purpose

This social media Policy establishes guidelines for the appropriate use of social media by
employees, representatives, and authorized users of the Town of Mayodan. The policy is
intended to ensure that all social media activities support the Town’s mission, maintain
public trust, and comply with applicable laws and regulations.

II. Deﬁnitions

   -    Content: Any posts, images, videos, audio, or other materials shared through social
        media platforms related to Town business.
   -    Employee: All Town of Mayodan personnel, including full-time, part-time, temporary
        employees, interns, volunteers, and contracted workers.
   -    Endorsement: Promotion of a product, service, or organization on a Town social
        media platform. All endorsements must be approved by the Town Manager or their
        designer.
   -    Social media: Online platforms used for communication and content sharing,
        including but not limited to Facebook, Instagram, Twitter/X, YouTube, LinkedIn, and
        similar applications.
   -    Social Networking: The use of online platforms to build relationships and
        communicate with others.

Scope

This policy applies to all Town of Mayodan employees. Employees should understand that
they always represent the Town, both on and off duty. Participation in social media should
reﬂect professionalism and awareness of how content may be perceived by the public.

IV. Public Records Law

All content related to Town business, including social media posts and interactions, is
subject to the North Carolina Public Records Law (N.C.G.S. § 132-1) and may be retained
and disclosed in accordance with state law.

V. Official Town Social Media Use

The Town of Mayodan uses social media to:

   •    Promote transparency in government operations

   •    Encourage civic engagement


   •   Share important updates, including emergency information

   •   Promote Town services, programs, and events

Authorized Users

Only employees authorized by the Town Manager may post or manage official Town social
media accounts.

Guidelines for Official Use

Authorized users must:

   •   Clearly identify themselves and their role when posting on behalf of the Town

   •   Ensure all information shared is accurate, professional, and timely

   •   Maintain respectful and courteous communication at all times

   •   Promptly correct errors when identiﬁed

   •   Use proper grammar, spelling, and tone

   •   Avoid engaging in arguments or unprofessional exchanges online

   •   Comply with copyright laws and only use approved content

Social media platforms should supplement the Town’s official website and direct users to it
as the primary source of information.

Unauthorized endorsements or promotions are prohibited unless approved by the Town
Manager.

Account Management

   •   Social media accounts must be regularly monitored and updated

   •   Comments should be reviewed, and platforms should include a notice such as:
       “Comments posted to this page will be monitored.”

   •   Departments should ensure coverage for account management during employee
       absences

   •   Responses to public inquiries should be timely and helpful

Personal Use of Social Media

The Town respects employees’ First Amendment rights; however, those rights are not
absolute when related to Town business.


Employees may use social media for personal purposes but must:

   •   Clearly distinguish personal opinions from official Town positions

   •   Avoid any appearance of speaking on behalf of the Town

   •   Exercise sound judgment and professionalism

   •   Comply with all Town policies, including the Code of Ethics and Personnel Policy

Inappropriate Use

Inappropriate social media use may result in disciplinary action, up to and including
termination. Examples include:

   •   Creating conﬂicts involving the Town, coworkers, or the public

   •   Interfering with workplace operations

   •   Posting harassing, discriminatory, or offensive content

   •   Damaging the Town’s reputation or public trust

   •   Disrupting delivery service to citizens

Excessive personal use of social media during work hours is also prohibited.

Prohibited Use

The following actions are strictly prohibited on both personal and official accounts:

   •   Sharing confidential or sensitive information
   •   Disclosing personal data (e.g., addresses, Social Security numbers, financial or
       medical information)
   •   Posting unlawful or inappropriate content
   •   Violating Town policies or Ethical Standards

Monitoring and Enforcement

   •   The Town reserves the right to monitor social media activity related to Town
       business. Employees should have no expectation of privacy when using Town-
       owned devices or networks.


   Reporting Violations

   •   Employees are encouraged to report suspected violations to a supervisor,
       Department Head, or Human Resources. All reports will be reviewed and addressed
       appropriately.

Content That May Be Shared

The Town may share community-related content that provides a clear public benefit,
including:

   •   Local events that are open to the public (festivals, markets, community gatherings)
   •   Grand openings and ribbon cuttings within Town limits
   •   Nonprofit initiatives, fundraisers, and charitable events
   •   Educational programs, public health information, and community services
   •   Partnerships or events involving the Town or affiliated organizations

All shared content must be accurate, appropriate, and relevant to the Mayodan
community.

Content That Will NOT Be Shared

The Town will not share:

   •   Political content, campaign materials, or endorsements of any candidate or issue
   •   Content that is discriminatory, offensive, or inappropriate
   •   Misleading, false, or unverifiable information
   •   Commercial advertisements that are solely promotional and do not provide a
       broader community benefit
   •   Content that violates copyright laws or lacks proper authorization

For-Profit Business Content

The Town may share limited content from for-profit businesses under the following
conditions:

   •   The content promotes a public event, grand opening, or activity open to the
       community
   •   The post is informational in nature and not purely an advertisement
   •   All businesses are given equal opportunity to be featured, with no favoritism shown

The Town reserves the right to limit the frequency of business-related posts to ensure
fairness and to prioritize official Town communications. When sharing content from
outside organizations or businesses, the following disclaimer will be included:


“The Town of Mayodan is sharing this information as a community service. The Town does
not endorse or sponsor the event, organization, or business referenced.”

To ensure effective communication and maintain an organized, engaging social media
presence, the Town of Mayodan will follow these guidelines for prioritizing and scheduling
content:

Prioritizing Urgent Information

Certain types of content require immediate attention and take precedence over other
posts, including:

   •   Road closures, traffic alerts, and detours
   •   Weather emergencies, natural disasters, or public safety alerts
   •   Health and safety notifications, such as water advisories or public health warnings

Urgent posts will be published promptly and may temporarily take priority over other
scheduled content.

Scheduling General Announcements & Events

   •   Non-urgent content, including events, community programs, and business
       highlights, should be scheduled in advance to maintain a consistent posting flow.
   •   Posts should be spaced to avoid overwhelming followers and to maximize visibility.
   •   Weekly or monthly planning is recommended to organize content by type and
       relevance.

Preventing Overcrowding & Excessive Posting

   •   The Town will limit the number of posts per day to maintain clarity and engagement.
   •   Group similar events or announcements into a single post when appropriate.
   •   Major announcements (e.g., holiday closures, important meetings) will be
       highlighted separately to ensure they are not lost in routine content.

Review & Adjustment

   •   Social media administrators will periodically review posting schedules and
       engagement to adjust timing and content prioritization.
   •   Scheduling flexibility is allowed to respond to urgent situations or unexpected
       community needs.


Social Media Content as Public Records

   •   All posts, comments, replies, messages, and attachments published on official
       Town social media accounts may be considered public records.

   •   This includes text, images, videos, and links shared on platforms such as Facebook,
       Twitter/X, Instagram, and YouTube.

   •   Administrators must treat content with the same care as other official records,
       maintaining integrity and accuracy.

Archiving Process

   •   All posts will be captured and archived using an approved method, such as:

          o   Platform-native archiving tools or download features

          o   Third-party social media archiving software that ensures a secure,
              searchable record

          o   Screenshots or PDFs for posts that are time-sensitive or contain community
              feedback

   •   Comments and direct messages that relate to Town business should also be
       retained as part of the record.

Retention Schedule

   •   Content should be retained for a minimum of ﬁve (5) years, in accordance with
       North Carolina public records requirements for municipal governments, unless
       longer retention is mandated by law for speciﬁc content (e.g., legal notices,
       contracts, ﬁnancial records).

   •   Archived content should include:

          o   Date and time of posting

          o   Author or account name

          o   Post content, including text, images, and links

          o   Any relevant engagement metrics (optional, for context)

Storage & Security

   •   Archived content should be stored on Town-managed servers or secure cloud
       platforms.


   •   Access to archived records must be limited to authorized personnel to protect the
       integrity of public records.

   •   Backups should be maintained to prevent loss due to technical failure or platform
       changes.

Compliance & Public Access

   •   Social media administrators must ensure all archived content is retrievable for
       public record requests in accordance with North Carolina Public Records Law.

   •   Any content removed from social media for corrections or errors must still be
       retained in the archive with documentation of the reason for removal.

Regular Review

   •   The Town will periodically review archiving processes to ensure compliance with
       legal requirements, platform changes, and technological updates.

   •   Staff will be trained in proper procedures for capturing, storing, and retrieving
       records from social media platforms.

                   NATIONAL PUBLIC WORKS WEEK PROCLAMATION
                                  May 17-23, 2026
                          “PEOPLE, PURPOSE, PRESENCE”

       WHEREAS, public works professionals focus on infrastructure, facilities, and services that are of vital
importance to sustainable and resilient communities and to the public health, high quality of life, and well-being of
the people of the Town of Mayodan; AND

        WHEREAS, these infrastructure, facilities, and services could not be provided without the dedicated efforts
of public works professionals, who are responsible for rebuilding, improving, and protecting our town’s transportation,
water supply, water treatment and solid waste systems, public buildings, and other structures and facilities essential
for our citizens; AND

       WHEREAS, it is in the public interest for the citizens, civic leaders, and children in the Town of Mayodan to
gain knowledge of and maintain an ongoing interest and understanding of the importance of Public Works and public
works programs in their respective communities; AND

        WHEREAS, the year 2026 marks the 66th annual National Public Works Week sponsored by the American
Public Works Association.

        NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT, the Mayodan Town Council do hereby designate the week
May 18–24, 2025, as National Public Works Week, and further extends its appreciation to our Public Works department
for the vital services they perform. We encourage all citizens to thank and celebrate our Public Works employees and
to recognize the substantial contributions they make to protecting our health, safety, and quality of life and for making
Town of Mayodan a great place to live, work, and visit.

PROCLAIMED this 11th day of May 2026.
